analysis: What changed vs the 4:00 AM brief: the Nvidia-led bounce is holding and slightly firming into the 5:00 AM hour — Nasdaq-100 futures +0.86% and NVDA +3.14% at ~7:30 AM ET, vs +1.17% futures and +2.9% NVDA at 4:00 AM. The new retail read is split in the same pattern as Target/Lowe's: TJX beat on revenue ($15.95B vs $15.84B est) and is up ~1.9% premarket, while Lowe's beat turns out to be tariff-refund-assisted (ex-refund EPS ~$2.76, below the $2.88 consensus) with a trimmed margin outlook, and the stock is falling — the third straight retail print where the reaction, not the beat, is the signal. Anthropic pricing tonight is the next AI-valuation test: reports of above-range pricing and ~7x oversubscription are single-source (WSJ/Bloomberg via secondary write-ups), so treat the >$80 talk as fragile until the official price lands. Megacaps outside Nvidia remain flat (AAPL and META slightly red, MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL up 0.1-0.7%), so the tape is still a single-stock bounce, not a broad turn. Oil and gold keep sliding together (WTI -2.59%, gold -2.37%) with the VIX easing to 24.19 — risk appetite returning rather than a safety bid. Signal vs noise: Nvidia's print and the retail split are signal; Anthropic pricing chatter and premarket wiggles in thin trading are noise until the open and the 2:00 PM ET FOMC minutes. Community: no qualifying thread — HN Algolia returned only older stories (latest relevant Nov 12 Anthropic IPO thread, 1007 points) and the Reddit site search returned nothing.

headlines.headline: Futures hold their gains into the 5:00 AM hour: at ~7:21 AM ET, S&P 500 futures +0.38%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.86%, Dow futures +0.03%. Tuesday closed S&P 500 7,340.53 (-1.03%), Nasdaq 24,328.38 (-0.74%), Dow 50,759.42 (-1.64%, -849 pts) — the fourth straight down day.
headlines.why_it_matters: A green open would snap the four-day losing streak, but the bounce is still Nvidia-led and narrow — breadth at the open decides whether it holds.

headlines.headline: Nvidia holding its post-earnings gain: $160.34 (+3.14%) at 7:32 AM ET, vs $155.46 Tuesday close. Q3 revenue $115.84B (+103% YoY) vs ~$109.1B expected, adj EPS $2.68 vs $2.47, Q4 guide $130B vs $125.25B consensus; AI hardware peers (CoreWeave, Marvell, Micron, AMD, Broadcom) up with it.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest overhang into the open is gone — the beat plus a raised guide is why futures flipped green after four straight down days.

headlines.headline: TJX beat on Q3 revenue before the open: $15.95B vs $15.84B expected (LSEG), as shoppers flocked to TJ Maxx and Marshalls for discounted apparel and home goods. Shares $132.27 (+1.86%) premarket at 7:16 AM ET (Finnhub).
headlines.why_it_matters: Third retail print of the morning and the cleanest beat — off-price strength reads as resilient consumer demand for value, not a spending collapse.

headlines.headline: Lowe's beat was tariff-refund-assisted and the margin outlook was trimmed: Q3 sales $22.8B (+9.3%), adj EPS $3.10 vs $2.88 expected, but $0.34 of that EPS came from tariff refunds — ex-refund ~$2.76, below expectations. Full-year sales outlook raised to ~$92.5B, but operating margin trimmed to ~11.1% from 11.2% and adj EPS held at ~$12.25. Shares down premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat the market is selling — strip out the one-off refund and the quarter missed, and the margin trim points to a softer Q4; the reaction, not the headline, is the signal.

headlines.headline: Take-Two +5.92% premarket: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow (Thu Nov 19); shares fell 4.47% on Tuesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A launch-eve bounce in a name that sold off into the event — premarket enthusiasm ahead of the biggest game launch of the year.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mostly flat outside Nvidia in premarket (Finnhub, ~7:15 AM ET): TSLA $383.07 (+0.78%), GOOGL $282.22 (+0.72%), AMZN $259.30 (+0.55%), MSFT $506.60 (+0.07%); AAPL $350.85 (-0.30%), META $616.32 (-0.41%). The four big AI spenders were up just ~0.6% on average at 4:27 AM ET while AI hardware names averaged +4.0%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Outside Nvidia and chips, the tape is flat — the premarket move is a single-stock story, not a megacap-wide turn.

headlines.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO tonight (after the close), first trade Thu Nov 19 on Nasdaq as ANT. Range $70-$78 (825M shares, up to ~$64.4B); reports say orders are ~7x oversubscribed and pricing could come in above $80, per WSJ/Bloomberg via secondary write-ups — single-source, unconfirmed until the official price lands. Seven strategic investors (Google, Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, TSMC) take $26B in a concurrent private placement at the IPO price.
headlines.why_it_matters: The next test of AI valuations after Nvidia's print — single-source, unconfirmed, treat the above-range talk as fragile; the official price tonight is what counts.
